Mach-O input support

by Alexander Panasenko · xrefcode.com
On this page
  1. Addresses and function evidence
  2. Linkage and reconstruction
  3. Fixture provenance

Available starting with v0.2.0. Published v0.1.0 binaries and the registry package at version 0.1.0 remain ELF-only.

Supported inputs: thin little-endian x86-64 Mach-O executables, dylibs and bundles with usable DWARF __eh_frame. An arm64 macOS host can analyze these x86-64 inputs. ARM64 input, 32-bit, fat/universal, encrypted, relocatable, kernel/cache/fileset and compact-unwind-only images are rejected. Input binaries are read and never executed.

Addresses and function evidence

The JSON/MCP identity uses format: "macho", architecture x86_64, and rva_basis: "macho_text_segment_vmaddr". Base is __TEXT.vmaddr; zero-file-size __PAGEZERO cannot become RVA base zero. LC_MAIN offsets and supported LC_UNIXTHREAD x86-64 states are normalized to VAs. No ASLR slide is inferred.

Typed function ranges still have range_origin: "eh_frame_fde": an unwind range is not proof of a whole source function. LC_FUNCTION_STARTS is compared with FDE starts; incomplete coverage is visible in warnings and info.format_details. Compact-only functions in mixed images return no_function through the strict typed API. Human CLI synthetic spans remain labelled synthetic and are bounded by the instruction section and next recorded function start.

File-backed linkage mappings remain readable by VA, but literal byte searches exclude __LINKEDIT, avoiding symbol-table spelling as a program-string hit. Function symbols keep raw linker spelling. Import names lose exactly one leading Mach-O underscore for the existing signature recognizer.

Linkage and reconstruction

Supported: indirect pointer/stub symbol slots; legacy dyld pointer rebase/bind/lazy/weak streams; x86-64 chained PTR_64 and PTR_64_OFFSET; chained import formats 1–3 with uncompressed names; export tries and defined external symbols. Unsupported threaded, authenticated, compressed and other pointer forms report incomplete metadata. Encoded chain words never become guessed target addresses; nonzero bind addends remain unresolved.

Legacy cursor movement follows dyld wrapping semantics, with strict bounds checked at every slot. File extents and VAs use checked arithmetic. Export traversal uses an explicit stack. Limits: one million decoded operations and 64 MiB total decoded name bytes. Malformed extents, duplicate singleton commands, invalid indices and cyclic export graphs fail explicitly.

Recorded Mach-O callers do not prove a closed return contract. Returns cannot be deleted or narrowed merely because those callers ignore them. Potential RAX/RDX output is preserved through the existing heuristic reconstruction. C, layouts, slices and types remain heuristic; inspect warnings and raw ASM.

The same loader serves CLI, JSON queries and local MCP. Use a returned FDE VA and an exact call-site instruction to inspect/slice it. See MCP and bounded investigations.

Fixture provenance

tests/fixtures/macho/ contains redistributable inputs from the included assembly and a simple C leaf. generate.py runs Xcode's xcrun clang on macOS and never executes outputs. JSON manifests record hashes, symbols, mapping geometry and known instruction targets. Legacy, chained, mixed-CFI, dylib and bundle profiles exercise the adapter. Linux tests use the checked-in inputs without needing a Mach-O linker.

Tests check identity, VAs, FDEs, references/calls, pointers, imports, exported and address-taken returns, a register-pair return, coverage gaps, malformed input, and CLI/MCP slice parity. Fixture regeneration is separate from normal test execution.
